_comment: All user-facing copy for Wizard Launcher. Edited without touching code; every consumer falls back to a built-in default if a key is missing, so a typo here degrades the text rather than breaking the launcher.

story.title: Witchcraft & Wizardry
story.tagline: A castle, rebuilt block by block.
paragraphs: Witchcraft and Wizardry is a hand-built adventure map: a full castle, its grounds, and a story you walk through rather than read. It was made by The Floo Network over several years, and it is played on a Minecraft 1.16.5 world.

Your launcher handles the awkward part. It runs the world on your own computer, bridges it to a modern Minecraft 1.20.1 client, installs the mods that make it run smoothly, and connects you - all from one button.
Nothing you do here touches the official Minecraft launcher, your existing worlds, or your saves.

steps.title: Welcome to the castle
steps.body: This launcher exists so that stepping into Witchcraft and Wizardry takes one click instead of an afternoon. There is nothing to configure - the next few screens just check that your computer is ready.

steps.title: Checking your computer
steps.body: A quick look at disk space, memory and Java. Anything the launcher can fix by itself, it will.

steps.title: How you want to play
steps.body: Sign in with Microsoft to use your real Minecraft name and skin, or just pick a name and play. You can change this at any time from the top right of the launcher.

steps.title: Performance
steps.body: The launcher has measured your RAM and picked memory settings that fit. You can change them later in Settings if the game feels slow.

steps.title: You're ready
steps.body: Press Begin the Journey when you are. The first launch downloads the castle and the game files, so it takes a few minutes - after that it is about fifteen seconds.

account_modes.title: Sign in with Microsoft
points: Other players see your actual Minecraft username and skin
Sign-in happens on Microsoft's own page - this launcher never sees your password
Your session is encrypted and stored in Windows Credential Manager

account_modes.title: Play as a guest
points: No sign-in, nothing stored, ready immediately
You choose the name that appears in game
The default Steve or Alex skin is used

getting_started.title: Sign in (optional)
getting_started.body: Click 'Guest Wizard' at the top right to use your real Minecraft name and skin. You can also just type a name and play.

getting_started.title: Press Begin the Journey
getting_started.body: The first launch downloads the castle and the game files - expect a few minutes on the first run and about 15 seconds after that.

getting_started.title: Wait for Minecraft to open
getting_started.body: The launcher starts the world server, opens the portal, then launches the game and connects you automatically.

getting_started.title: When you're done
getting_started.body: Just close Minecraft. The launcher shuts the world down and saves it for you.

faq.question: Do I need to own Minecraft?
faq.answer: Yes. Wizard Launcher does not include Minecraft and never downloads a copy of the game you have not paid for. It downloads the map and the mods, and uses your own account to run the game.

faq.question: Does this affect my normal Minecraft?
faq.answer: No. The launcher keeps its own game folder, its own mods and its own worlds. Your existing worlds, servers and settings are untouched.

faq.question: Can my friends join me?
faq.answer: Turn on 'Allow friends on my network to join' in Settings, then give them your computer's local IP address. Only people on the same Wi-Fi or LAN can connect - the launcher never opens your world to the internet.

faq.question: Where are my files kept?
faq.answer: In your AppData folder. Open Settings and use 'Open game folder' to go straight there. Earlier versions kept them in Documents; if you are upgrading, the launcher moved them for you and left a note behind.

faq.question: How much disk space do I need?
faq.answer: About 4 GB free: roughly 1.5 GB for the castle and resource pack, and the rest for the Minecraft client, the mods and a Java runtime.

faq.question: Is my Microsoft password safe?
faq.answer: The launcher never sees it. Sign-in happens on Microsoft's own website and only a token comes back, which is encrypted before it is stored. Log files are scrubbed of tokens before anything is written to disk.

faq.question: Why does it need Java?
faq.answer: Minecraft and the world server both run on Java. The launcher finds a suitable version on your computer, and downloads an official one from Mojang if there is not one.

faq.question: Can I keep playing if I close the launcher?
faq.answer: Yes. Close the launcher any time after Minecraft has opened - a small helper keeps watching, and shuts the world down and saves it when you quit the game.

troubleshooting.symptom: It says a port is already in use
troubleshooting.cause: Something else is holding port 25565 or 25566 - usually a world server from a previous session that did not shut down.
steps: Press Stop in the launcher; that releases both ports.
If it persists, close any other Minecraft server running on this PC.
As a last resort, restart your computer.

troubleshooting.symptom: Minecraft opened but did not connect
troubleshooting.cause: The client started before the portal finished opening, or you closed the connection screen.
steps: Open the Multiplayer menu - 'Witchcraft and Wizardry' is already in the server list.
Click it to join.
If it shows as offline, go back to the launcher and press Stop, then Play again.

troubleshooting.symptom: The game stutters or freezes every few seconds
troubleshooting.cause: The world server and the game are competing for memory on the same machine.
steps: Open Settings and lower the world server memory by 512 MB.
Turn off background animations in Settings to free up a CPU core.
Close other heavy programs - browsers with many tabs are the usual culprit.
Lower the render distance inside Minecraft's own video settings.

troubleshooting.symptom: It cannot find Java, or the download fails
troubleshooting.cause: No suitable Java runtime is installed and the automatic download was blocked.
steps: Check your internet connection and firewall, then press Play again.
Or install Java 17 from https://adoptium.net and restart the launcher.
Antivirus software sometimes blocks the download - allow Wizard Launcher through it.

troubleshooting.cause: An unstable connection, or something between you and the download server interfering with HTTPS.
steps: Press Play again - a partial download is resumed rather than restarted.
Try a different network, such as a phone hotspot.
Temporarily disable 'HTTPS scanning' in your antivirus.
If it still fails, use Clear Cache and let it download fresh.

troubleshooting.symptom: I want to start completely over
steps: 'Clear Cache' erases the world, your progress and the downloaded game files - everything is downloaded again on the next launch.
'Clear Player Data' only resets your inventory, position and advancements, keeping everything that was built.
Player data is backed up automatically before it is reset, so a mistake is recoverable.
Use 'Create diagnostic report' below - it collects the logs and your system details into one file.
Attach that file to a GitHub issue with the Report Issue button.
Passwords and tokens are removed from everything the launcher writes.
